entities.name: Aphrodite
entities.summary: Goddess associated with love and desire, with distinct genealogies in Hesiod and Homer.

entities.name: Dione
entities.summary: Mother of Aphrodite in Homer’s Iliad; the poem does not identify her as a specific Hesiodic Oceanid.

entities.name: Erichthonius of Athens
entities.summary: Earth-born early king of Athens raised by Athena, distinct from the Trojan of the same name.

entities.name: Praxithea
entities.summary: Naiad and wife of Erichthonius of Athens, mother of Pandion I.

entities.name: Pandion I of Athens
entities.summary: Son of Erichthonius and Praxithea and father of Erechtheus.

entities.name: Zeuxippe
entities.summary: Sister of Praxithea and mother of Erechtheus by Pandion I.

entities.name: Atthis
entities.summary: Daughter of Cranaus and alternative mother of Erichthonius of Athens in Apollodorus.

entities.name: Praxithea
entities.summary: Wife of Erechtheus and daughter of Phrasimus and Diogenia; distinct from the Naiad wife of Erichthonius.

lineages.notes: She emerges in sea foam around severed genitals; not a normal biological birth or a two-parent union.
Dione is explicitly mother and Zeus called father in the poem; Homer does not explicitly identify this Dione with Hesiod’s Oceanid.
Hephaestus’s seed falls on Earth after Athena wipes it away; Earth produces the child, whom Athena raises. The text also reports an alternative parentage.
An alternative reported before the Earth-born story; keep separate.
Do not conflate Erechtheus with Erichthonius merely because early traditions sometimes overlap.
The source also names her mother Pedias in 3.14.5.

relationships.notes: They share Melinoë’s tent at the Crossroads; non-spoiler game relationship. No claim about Dora’s hidden identity.
Erechtheus marries Praxithea. She is distinct from the Praxithea married to Erichthonius.

coverage.group: Aphrodite, with two separately attributed origin traditions
coverage.notes: Two selected accounts, not an exhaustive list.
